characters.name: As a Whole
characters.description: Accidental Hero: Shaggy and Scoobyaccidentally cause the other members of Mystery, Inc. to fail to capture the Luna Ghost at the beginning, but still manage to get the Ghost captured by accident when they are stuck in a barrel and hanging from a hook, and end up swinging into the Ghost. Achievements in Ignorance: Per the standard with the iconic duo, Scooby and Shaggy trip and stumble their way to victory without fully knowing what they're doing. More so Shaggy in this movie,remaining the only character who avoided both capture and having his soul sucked out using the pincer. Adaptational Jerkass: One of the major criticisms of the first film is that the gang are....really rough around the edges to put it one way. Fred, Daphne, and Velma spend much of the film arguing, Scooby punches Fred in the face, Shaggy suggests after Fred and Velma are captured by monsters that he, Scooby and Daphne let them get eaten (the cartoon version of Shaggy is a coward, but he's not the kind of person that would abandon his friends), and a flashback shows them abandoning Scrappy — Scooby's nephew — in the middle of the desert. And Scrappy himself goes from being annoying but competent to full on Big Bad whose bite is nothing compared to his bark. Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: When Shaggy and Scooby initially decline the invitation to Spooky Island.Shaggy:Oh, Scoob and I don't go near any place with "spooky", "haunted", "forbidden", or "creepy" in the name.Scooby:Or "hydrocolonic".Shaggy:Right, or "hydrocolonic". But that's for a totally different reason, man. Better as Friends:Shaggy and Velmadecide they're better off not dating at the end of the fourth film.

characters.name: Scooby-Doo
characters.description: The title character of the franchise, Scooby-Doo is a talking Great Dane who is the gang'sTeam Pet. Although almost always cowardly and hungry, he more often than not comes through in helping his human friends solve mysteries. Accidental Athlete: In "Ghastly Goals", he becomes part of the Brazilian soccer team as he tries to retrieve a soccer ball endowed with a formula that makes it bounce stronger from a beast called an Eshu. Action Pet: Scooby can beveryheroic when he needs to be. Adaptational Badass: In some incarnations, mostly the movies andScooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated, he is portrayed as braver and more willing to face his enemies head-on. Adaptational Jerkass: InScooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporatedhe is more of a jerk, constantly fights with Velma, and talks more often, which adds to the attempt in developing the characters.He gets better, of course.

characters.name: Shaggy Rogers
characters.description: Scooby's laid-back owner and best friend, Shaggy is just as cowardly and hungry as his pet but is still a dedicated detective when he's not eating or running from an apparant danger. Adaptational Attractiveness: Not as much as Velma, butWhat's New, Scooby-Doo?and the live-action films do feature a Shaggy more attractive than the skinny, lanky original Shaggy. In the theatrical live-action movies, he is played by theTall, Dark, and HandsomeMatthew Lillardand in the live-action TV Movies, he is played by thePretty BoyNick Palatas. Adaptational Badass: In some movies and inScooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated. Some likeMortal Kombat Legends: Battle of the RealmsandMultiVersushave gone fullAscended Memeand made Shaggy a being with the powers of a physical god, in a nod to the fans perceiving him as a Super Saiyan-like figure. Ascended Meme: A joke amongst the fandom that's occurred sinceScooby-Doo! Legend of the Phantosauris that Shaggy is secretly the most powerful being in the universe.Mortal Kombat Legends: Battle of the RealmsandMultiVersusfeatured him with such powers. While it was never explained how that wound up happening in the former, the latter gave Shaggy those powers inan official backstory—he was mystery solving with the gang, found a mysterious crystal, andate itwhen he mistook it for food. When he woke up, he gained unimaginable power. Badass Driver: Not as readily apparent as Fred'sbadass driving skills(since Fred is usually the one driving), butScooby-Doo! and the Reluctant Werewolfshows that Shaggy is an accomplished race car driver, somewhat akin toSpeed Racer. He also managed to successfully maneuver the Mystery Machine around other cars and over ariverwithout crashing or hitting the water, at high speed, with no breaks inScooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico. On very rare occasions he has crossed intoBackseat Driverterritory, reaching over and grabbing the wheel if Fred loses control of the van.

characters.name: Velma Dinkley
characters.description: The gang's bespectacled "brains", Velma puts whatever tools she has with her to good use to find the culprits behind every mystery. Adaptational Attractiveness: Varies, but she gets hit with this semi-often. While never truly ugly, Velma was traditionally average weight, with a short-and-stout appearance, tacky haircut, and a relatively plain face. Starting withZombie Island, this started to change somewhat,especiallyinWhat's New, Scooby-Doo?and the movies (much like Shaggy), where she's made very petite with a tiny waist and anhourglass figure, with a cute-as-a-button face to boot◊(taken from thissceneinScooby-Doo! Camp Scare). And in the live-action films, she's played by very attractive actresses. The most recent animated movies fuse these two somewhat, andMystery Inc.also splits the difference – Velma sports a cuter, more stylized version of her original appearance, complete with little bows in her hair. She didn't gain extra weight and freckles until a bit later after the debut so her new attractiveness is a bit closer to how she originally looked. Adaptational Jerkass: InScooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated, she is more cynical, self-centered, vain, andsarcastic, similar to the titular protagonist ofDaria. Most of these changes, however, are to do with her being written a lot more like an actual teenager would act, andjustifiablegiven that theCrapsack WorldofMystery Incorporatedisharshtowards anyone with a semblance of decency. Shetakes a level in kindnessthanks toCharacter Development. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: InScooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated, she and Scooby generally don't get along very well, often feuding over Shaggy and generally being nasty towards each other — to the point that in one episode, when Scooby is thrown in prison over a crime that he didn't commit, Velma doesn't care all that much because now she has Shaggy all to herselfnotefor obvious reasons, he winds up dumping her at the end. Now, let's compare that to previous productions likeA

characters.name: Daphne Blake
characters.description: A fashionable young woman from a wealthy family, Daphne is as dedicated to solving mysteries as the rest of the gang no matter how prone to danger she tends to be. Abandoned Catchphrase: Daphne does not actually say "Jeepers!" throughout the entire run ofA Pup Named Scooby-Doo, and would not again untilScooby-Doo and the Cyber Chasea full decade later. Action Girl: Later adaptations have Daphne display multiple, high-skill action abilities as if she's the franchise's own version ofLara Croft. Theroutinein nearly every direct-to-video film is to have a scene or two that showcases her action skills, and often the rest of the gang being surprised. The Lara Croft similarities get the ultimate presentation in the alternate (very, veryalternate) continuity ofScooby Apocalypse, which has Daphne (and only her among the team, at first) even being exceptionally skilled with every type of gun, something never permitted (of course) anywhere else in the franchise. Adaptational Badass: Overall, Daphne has been portrayed as more badass in later adaptations than in earlier ones, but she still flits between being anAction GirlandDamsel in Distressin each production. Adaptational Curves: Daphne'salready lovely bodyis even more curvaceous and buxom inWhat's New, Scooby-Doo?than in previous incarnations. This is taken even further inScooby-Doo and Guess Who?, where she becomes anImpossible Hourglass Figure.

characters.name: Fred Jones
characters.description: The leader of Mystery Incorporated, Fred drives the gang around on the Mystery Machine to catch culprits. Abandoned Catchphrase: As explained below, inThe New Scooby-Doo Movies, Fred briefly had the catchphrase "Creepers!", possibly as a counterpart to Daphne's "Jeepers!", but it was never used again. Adaptational Badass: InScooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporatedwhere his traps are far more effective and have a greater success ratio, without losing their complexity. In addition to all this, he has the most physical prowess of the gang and has occasionally used that to his advantage. Adaptational Dumbass: He was originally the second smartest in the gang but has Taken a Level in Dumbass ever since Daphne started becoming more competent. Essentially Daphne took a good portion of his leadership skills and intelligence. Some incarnations exaggerate this even more. He seems to have returned to his original portrayal inBe-Cool, Scooby-Doowhile Daphne was turned into aCloud Cuckoolanderwith mental issues.InA Pup Named Scooby-Doo, he's turned into a moronic conspiracy theorist that reads too much of a satirical newspaper called "The National Exaggerator" which he takes seriously and where he blames every misdeed on the neighborhood bully, Red Herring. InA Pup Named Scooby-Doo, he's turned into a moronic conspiracy theorist that reads too much of a satirical newspaper called "The National Exaggerator" which he takes seriously and where he blames every misdeed on the neighborhood bully, Red Herring.

characters.name: Scrappy-Doo
characters.description: Scooby's more courageous nephew. The one who yells, "Let me at 'em!", when he sees theMonster of the Week. To prevent spoilers, some of Scrappy's tropes from the 2002 movieScooby-Doo (2002)are not listed here and are instead listed in the live-action characters list. Notorious for being theTrope NamerforThe Scrappy. Adaptational Jerkass: In the Archie comics, though arguably he's aJerk with a Heart of Gold. Adaptational Personality Change: In the Archie comics, he's snarky, abrasive, temperamental, rude, and opportunistic. His devotion to his uncle still remains, though. Adults Are More Anthropomorphic:Inverted, Scrappy stands on his hind legs most of the time, while Scooby walks on all fours. Ambiguously Absent Parent: His father's identity and his mother's whereabouts are unknown. Maybe this is why he latches on to Scooby so much.

characters.name: Scooby-Dum
characters.description: Scooby-Doo's cousin, who appeared inThe Scooby-Doo Show. A grey Great Dane who definitely lives up to his name. Has not been seen or mentioned since the final iteration of the original series ended in the mid-80s. He is a member of the Scooby Doobies in the Laff-A-Lympics. Adapted Out: He and Sooey Pig do not appear in theLaff-A-Lympicscomics by Marvel Comics. Advertised Extra: Scooby-Dum is featured in the opening sequence ofThe Scooby-Doo Show, but only appears in four out of the forty total episodes. Ascended Extra: He was a recurring team member onLaff-A-Lympics. Catchphrase: "Dum dum dum DUM!" (fromLudwig van Beethoven'sFifth Symphony.)

characters.name: Flim-FlamMcScam
characters.description: Flim-Flam joined the cast inThe 13 Ghosts of Scooby-Doo. The only character who couldpossiblybe more disliked than Scrappy at the time. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: He'll go from trying to con someone to screaming "Please don't hurt me!" in all of two seconds flat if they call him out on what he's doing. Shaggy evenlampshades itwhen he tells Flim-Flam to skip the begging and justrun. Beta Couple: He was basically the Shaggy to Scrappy Doo's Scooby. The Bus Came Back: Flim-Flam finally came back after 34 years of absence inThe Curse of the 13th Ghost. Character Development: By his return inThe Curse of the 13th Ghost, the young man is shown to have outgrown his tendency to con others and makes an honest living selling ghost hunting equipment and souvenirs.

characters.name: Yabba-Doo
characters.description: The Ace: Yabba-Doo is this, since he's consistently brave to the point that Dusty and Scrappy trail behind. Catchphrase: "Yippity-Yabbity-Doo!" Logic would dictate that it would be "Yabba-Dabba-Doo",but someone else already says that... Cowboy: He's a cowboy. Heterosexual Life-Partners: He and Dusty are close friends of the same gender, much like Shaggy and Scooby. Messy Hair: His fur is rather unkempt, in contrast to Scooby's.

characters.name: Deputy Dusty
characters.description: Blind Without 'Em: Subverted, unlike another, a more well-known character in the Scooby franchise. Dusty's round, wire-rimmed specs are seen but never factor into any of the plots. Composite Character: Of Shaggy and Fred-having the former's cowardice and the latter's authoritativeness. In appearance, he has Shaggy's skinny build and Fred's clean-cut look. Friend on the Force: He's a main character in the Scrappy-Doo and Yabba Doo shorts, and Tumbleweed's sheriff. In Touch with His Feminine Side: Very much so. He's timid, bakes Chili Snacks, and gets embarrassed when his shirt gets blown off during a motorcycle chase — though he's just as heroic as Scrappy and Yabba.

characters.name: Vincent Van Ghoul
characters.description: The Ace: Regarded as the world's most powerful warlock and aCool Old Guyto boost. Adaptational Wimp: InMystery Inc., he has no magic powers, being just an actor. Ancient Keeper: While not quite as decrepit as most examples, he was guarding the Chest of Demons... Big Good: InThe 13 Ghosts of Scooby-Doo Cool Old Guy: He appears to be a dapper gentleman in his 60s, he's actually much older (see below), and short fuse and unreasonable demands aside, he's nothing but helpful to the gang and has a lot of flare.

characters.name: The Hex Girls
characters.description: An all-girl rock band with a Goth motif, extremely popular in theScooby-verse. They first appeared inScooby-Doo! and the Witch's Ghost, and have popped up from time to time since, including inMystery Inc., where they inadvertently have a major impact on the main gang's character arcs. Adaptational Protagonist: Thorn holds the mantle of main character inThe Hex Girls: A Rogue Thornas opposed to Scooby as usual. Age Lift: The Hex girls arguably were in their 20s inScooby-Doo! and the Witch's Ghost, but all three were aged down to teens inThe Hex Girls: A Rogue Thorn. All There in the Manual: A few official concept artworks prior to "The Witch's Ghost" imply thatthey've been friends since childhood. Ambiguously Brown: Luna, made more confusing whenLegend of the VampireandWhat's Newmake her just as white as the others whileMystery IncorporatedandGuess Whomake her darker.

characters.name: Red Herring
characters.description: A neighborhood bully in Coolsville and Freddie's prime suspect in any mystery inA Pup Named Scooby-Doo. Arch-Enemy: Freddiereallywants him to be the criminal. The Bully: Largely spends his time insulting Scooby and friends. Butt-Monkey: He often gets in trouble or humiliated. He deserves it for being a bully. Catchphrase: He often says "That's not very funny" whenever the gang laughs at him getting his well-deserved comeuppance.

characters.name: Jenkins
characters.description: Crazy-Prepared: The one time he couldn't help Daphne (in "Dog Gone Scooby"), he had a backup butler named Dawson on call to help in his place. Hyper-Competent Sidekick: He's very capable in a lot of facets, including piloting a helicopter (as seen in "Horror of the Haunted Hairpiece"). Speak of the Devil: If he so much thinks you called for him, he'll come without hesitation. In "The Return of Commander Cool", Velma said "Jinkies", and he immediately popped up. Undying Loyalty: He will help the gang no matter how strange the request, even if it's something like doing aWild Takein Daphne's place. The only time he didn't help was in "Dog Gone Scooby", and that was because he couldn't be in two places at once — instead, theirotherbutler Dawson shows up instead, explaining that Jenkins is busy doing Daphne's shopping. Wild Take: In "Terror, Thy Name is Zombo", Daphne summons him to react to the ghost of the clown Zombo by doing a wild take in her place (or as she puts it, "Be scared for me"), since she's just had her hair done and doesn't want to mess it up.

characters.name: Googie
characters.description: Shaggy's girlfriend inThe Reluctant Werewolf. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She only appears inThe Reluctant Werewolf, though the movie had aSequel Hook. Had there been further installments, one could assume that she would've made further appearances in those. Nice Girl: She's a very amiable person. Satellite Character: She mostly exists so that there could be a female main character inThe Reluctant Werewolf. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: For Daphne, asThe Reluctant Werewolfwas released a couple of years after Daphne's last appearance inThe 13 Ghosts of Scooby-Doo. Like Daphne before her, Googie is a kind redheaded female protagonist that exists for female viewers and is partnered up with Shaggy, Scooby, and Scrappy as they encounter the supernatural on their adventures.

characters.name: Monsters and Ghosts in general
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: In the various video games, where it's required that they be more hostile and antagonistic.noteFor example, inNight of 100 Frights, the Space Kook gains aRay Gun. InUnmasked, the pterodactyl can breathfire. Adaptational Costume Change: In the Bugsy Reading System take on the story, Buck Masters's disguise as an Indian Witch Doctor was changed to a ghost miner seemingly to remove offensive stereotyping. Affably Evil: Bluestone the Great, the illusionist revealed to be the "ghost" of Vazquez castle in "Hassle in the Castle"; he doesn't even give aYou Meddling Kidsspeech but is cooperative enough to be a good sport when he's allowed to give an encore demonstration of how he managed to impersonate the ghost when the police take him away. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Too many to count, up to (and including) Charlie the Funland Robot, the Dinkley 2000, the Night Ghoul of London, the animatronics of Cyber Gulch, and Shari, a computerized "house of the future". Notably, some of these actuallyarestraight-up examples, Aliens Are Bastards: Natch. The Space Kook, the first of many other villainous "extra"-terrestrials, is an alien and it's just as troublesome as the other monsters they chase.

characters.name: What's New Scooby Doo monsters
characters.description: An Ice Person: The Snow Creature appears to be made of ice and snow. Eventually it turns out to be mechanical, and all its components inside are made of transparent material to sell the illusion. Tank-Tread Mecha: For most of its episode, the snow creature's feet are covered by snow. The climactic chase reveals its feet are really treads,just moments before it's discovered to be a robot.

characters.name: The  13 Ghosts from the Chest of Demons
characters.description: Fusion Dance: When confined to the Chest of Demons, they tend to combine into various demonic forms. Monster of the Week: Similar to what was done with the criminals disguised as monsters in most continuities,The 13 Ghosts of Scooby-Doocontinued the format of the gang fighting a different antagonist in every episode with the twist that the supernatural beings were now genuinely supernatural. Obviously Evil: With the exception ofNekara, all of them either look evil, haveevil-sounding names, or both. Our Demons Are Different: Several of them are referred to as demons. They border on being flat-outGods of Evil. Sealed Evil in a Can: They were all imprisoned in the Chest of Demons before Scooby and Shaggy were tricked into opening the Chest of Demons by Bogel and Weerd. The series' goal was then to recapture the 13 escaped ghosts.

characters.name: Del Chillman
characters.description: First featured inScooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster, and later seen again inChill Out, Scooby-Doo!. Agent Mulder: He believes in the Loch Ness Monster, and insists that the highland games are angering it and that it needs protection. Once "Nessie was a no-show", he moves up to the Himalayas to search for the Abominable Snowman. The Bus Came Back: He gives up on Nessie and moved to the Himalayas where he became the mountain's DJ much to Shaggy and Scooby's happy surprise. Cool Car: His van, which was essential in the"Scooby-Doo" Hoaxafter it was stolen and used for one of the land Loch Ness Monsters. Good Samaritan: In the Himalayas, he's quick to save Shaggy and Scooby when he finds them lost and freezing, and then to let them enjoy the comforts of his weather station.

characters.name: Shannon Blake
characters.description: A young Scottish woman who also happens to be Daphne's cousin—Shannon lives in Blake Castle (the ancestral home of Daphne's Scottish side of the family) and is the primary caretaker for it. Boyish Short Hair: She has very short hair, which contrasts with Daphne'sLong Hair Is Feminine—also, when it comes to her clothes (which are still very stylish), Shannon dresses in a much more tomboyish way compared to her American-cousin. Cute Clumsy Girl: Much like Daphne, Shannon's (presumably) this—also, according to Shannon, the clumsiness that led to Daphne being referred to as "danger-prone" is a hereditary trait for the Blakes (at least when it comes to the Scottish side of Daphne's family). Damsel in Distress: Gets captured with Daphne by the villain's lackeys. Sixth Ranger: Accompanies the gang for most of their adventures in the film.

characters.name: Fiona Pembrooke
characters.description: An academic who believes in the Loch Ness monster. Agent Mulder: Pembrooke firmly believes the Loch Ness Monster exists. The Alleged Car: Or rather a boat. Her research vessel is in pretty crummy shape. It's camouflage for a "monster" submarine docked underneath. Anti-Villain: She is revealed to be responsible for the movie's"Scooby-Doo" Hoax, because she was frustrated by Sir Ian's persistent disbelief in the creature's existence. Casting Gag: Her voice-actress, singer Sheena Easton, is genuinely from Scotland.

characters.name: Angus and Colin Haggart
characters.description: Two mischief-loving brothers competing in the Highland Games. Anti-Villain: They are revealed to have assisted Professor Pembrooke with her"Scooby-Doo" Hoaxsimply because they believed it was a good prank. Jerk Jock: More lightly and playfully. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: They mess around, goof off, and tease Shannon about worrying the Loch Ness Monster will eat them when they go swimming in the loch; but after the monster causes the boat to crash, they both go over to Shannon to check if she's okay. The Prankster: The only thing they seem passionate about is jokes, whether on each other or others.

characters.name: Lachlan Haggart
characters.description: The local innkeeper and Colin and Angus's dad. Agent Scully: He doesn't believe in the Loch Ness monster but promotes the legend to attract tourists. Sports Dad: He relishes the games and the idea of his sons competing in them. Why Couldn't You Be Different?: At one point, he looks towards the sky and says, "I asked for jocks and you gave me jokers instead." And near the end of the movie, where his sons admit that they had no real interest in the Highland Games and went along with Dr. Pembrooke's scheme because they thought it would make a good prank, Mr. Haggart mutters, "I should've prayed harder for daughters."

characters.name: Sir Ian Locksley
characters.description: Academic Athlete: Sir Ian is a skinny, gray-haired museum director and scholar who is also the head judge for the Highland games and can throw a thick caber quite a distance. Agent Scully: Ian disbelieves in the Loch Ness Monster, until the end. Cool Ship: He has a very large and heavily armed research vessel which he brings to guard the loch against any threats as the games approach. Lean and Mean: A relatively intense, thin man who is easily angered by the mention of the loch Ness monster. Man in a Kilt: He proudly wears a kilt everywhere.

characters.name: DuncanMacGubbin
characters.description: The local dock master and a firm believer in the monster. Cursed with Awesome: He holds the record for most Loch Ness monster sightings but claims to be bothered by this. Doomsayer: He appears in the middle of rain or fog to give loud, ominous warnings about the monster's presence. Fish Eyes: His eyes are always wide and looking in opposite directions. Insistent Terminology: Duncan gets very irritated when Fred says "lake" instead of "loch."

characters.name: Mcintyre
characters.description: The first mate aboard Ian'sCool Ship. Abandon Ship: He and his cronies dive overboard as the ship is run aground and don't appear again. Beard of Evil: He's a villain with a decent beard across his face. Evil Redhead:McIntyreis a redhead who betrays the gang and Sir Ian. Greed: He wants to capture and sell the Loch Ness Monster.

characters.name: Amelia von Butch
characters.description: An infamous treasure hunter who is out to steal Cleopatra's crown after her tomb is discovered by Velma and Omar. Adventure Archaeologist: Deconstructed. She has a PHD in archaeology, but she's more focused on finding treasure than she is at preserving history and has no problem breaking a few laws in search of her goal. Big Bad: She's after Cleopatra's treasure, but surprisingly, she isn't the one behind the"Scooby-Doo" Hoax. Bound and Gagged: When she is captured by the mummies she has her hands tied behind her back. She manages to escape during the gang's assault on the tomb. Later when she runs out of the tomb she sets off one of Fred’s traps and is wrapped up in a rug and hoisted off the ground. She doesn’t escape this time. Corrupted Character Copy: She's basically an evilLara Croft.

characters.name: Prince Omar Karam
characters.description: A Middle-Eastern prince and Velma's archeological partner. Royals Who Actually Do Something: He's working to restore a lost archeological treasure and personally helps lead the"Scooby-Doo" Hoaxto scare off tomb robbers. Taken for Granite: He gets turned to stone but it's all a hoax. Uptown Girl: Gender Inverted and downplayed; he and Velma have someShip Teasethat naturally never turns into anything permanent. Velma is a workaday American girl while Omar is a royal Egyptian guy.

characters.name: Rock Rivers
characters.description: A canceled reality TV show host trying to get back on track with the mummy story. Alliterative Name:RockRivers. Enlightened Self-Interest: He ultimately helps Velma and Omar, although partially because it ensures him a good story. Nightmare Fetishist: Gushes about the curse and mummies excitedly, although mainly just because of the rating potential. Red Herring: Played with. Despite having a motive, he isn't behind the hoax of Cleopatra's tomb, but he is providing help to the people who are.

characters.name: Ahmal Ali Akbar AKA Triple A
characters.description: A Bedouin traveler who aids the gang. All-Powerful Bystander: He isn't an undercover cop, a disguised villain, or anything of the like, just an ordinary man who gives the team a lift and keeps showing up to give them aid at the right time. Bedouin Rescue Service: He's introduced in this manner, and even has a bunch of camels. Casting Gag: Not thefirsttimeOded Fehrhas played a desert nomad with a falcon companion named Horus. Good Samaritan: He gives the team a ride when they’re stranded in the desert and later nurses Fred and Daphne back to health after they are attacked and drugged.

characters.name: Campbell and Natasha
characters.description: Two of Von Butch's team, and the only two to escape their initial encounter with the mummy. All There in the Script: Their names are revealed in the credits, but are never spoken onscreen. Ambiguously Brown: Campbell's skin is fairly dark, but it could just be well-tanned. Badass Boast: When told about the threat of the undead, Campbell says if they encounter them;Then they won't stayundead for long. The Brute: Campbell is the most imposing of Van Butch's team and effortlessly crushes a cellphone with his bare hand.

characters.name: Hotep/Armin Granger
characters.description: The leader of the Lost City cult, a group of people choosing to live as though they were Ancient Egyptians. Evil Chancellor: Acts as this to Scooby when the Lost City believes that Scooby is their legendary Pharaoh Ascoobis. Gadgeteer Genius: He is a brilliant civil engineer who has made a dam to divert a large portion of the Nile River to the Lost City. He also uses a gigantic robotic scorpion for entertainment in the city's arena. High Priest: He portrays himself as being the high priest of the Lost City. Monumental Theft: With his illegal dams, he has stolen a portion of the Nile, causing a drought.

characters.name: Pemba
characters.description: A Tibetan mountain guide. Big Brother Instinct: Pemba becomes very upset at the idea that his sister Minga is in danger (although as a kid, he was aBig Brother Bullyin a mildly teasing way). Native Guide: Pemba leads climbing expeditions up Mount Everest and has enough respect for local superstitions to avoid certain areas.

characters.name: Minga
characters.description: Pemba's music-obsessed sister. Annoying Younger Sibling: Minga's obsession with western music, (faked)Arbitrary Skepticismabout the monster, and insistence on tagging along with the expedition cause her brother to exasperatedly say that she's as stubborn as a yak. Anti-Villain: Minga is behind the"Scooby-Doo" Hoax, but only because she wants to give her cryptozoologist crush a reason to stay in the area. Aroused by Their Voice: She's in love with a DJ she's never seen face-to-face. Official Couple: With Dell Chillman.

characters.name: Alphone Lafleur
characters.description: A hunter obsessed with the Abominable Snowman. Egomaniac Hunter:LaFleuris a boastful professional hunter obsessed with bagging the Abominable Snowman but suffers scores ofAmusing Injuriesin the process. He tricks Shaggy and Scooby into accompanying him to serve as "the bait no monster can refuse." That being said, most to all of his traps are non-lethal ones (indicating he plans to take the monster alive), and he abandons his hunt after believing that the Snowman may have saved his life. Expy: His beard, personality, actions, intentions, andButt-Monkeymishaps make him a version ofYosemite Sam, with a touch ofYukon Corneliusconsidering both his design and relationship with the Abominable Snowman. Hoist by His Own Petard:LaFleuris injured by several of his traps.

characters.name: Professor Jeffries
characters.description: A scientist who is exploring Mount Everest. Adventurer Archaeologist: Jeffries is a bold and fit man who is obsessed with finding the lost kingdom of Shangri-La. Ultimately, he's a negative example of the trope, as he's mainly concerned with padding his own pockets from a diamond mine that isn't his to take. Eviler than Thou:Of the film's other villains, Minga is anAnti-VillainandLaFleurhas aHeel Realization. Meanwhile,Jeffries's greedy looting is portrayed completely unsympathetically, and in the final act, he's more violent and unrepentant than the other two. Evil Brit: He has a British accent. Greed: Jeffries's obsession with lining his own pockets is sinister and all-consuming.

characters.name: The Goblin King
characters.description: The titular character ofScooby-Doo! and the Goblin King, who's... not exactly what others think he's like. Big Bad: Subverted. He appears to be the Big Bad of the film but in truth he is not this. He was just trying to get his daughter back from Krudsky, who agreed to give her back in order to get his staff and have real magic powers. Dark Is Not Evil: Built-up as a scary and evil being throughout the movie. Turns out, past his scary demeanor, the guy is quite benevolent as long as you don't cross him. Disc-One Final Boss: He initially appeared to be the main threat of the story given that he was big, scary and was believed to have played the role of turning some of Scooby and Shaggy’s friends into real monsters. However, once Daphne, Fred and Velma capture the King, Krudsky becomes theBig Badby taking his staff and becomes the threat and turning the king into a goose. Good All Along: Rather than wanting Fairy Princess Willow for some nefarious purpose as everyone assumed, the Goblin King is actually Willow's dad and is making the trade with Krudsky simply to ensure she is returned to him safely.

characters.name: Fairy Princess Willow
characters.description: A fairy princess featured inScooby-Doo! and the Goblin King. She also happens to be the Goblin King's daughter. Damsel in Distress: Kidnapped by Krudsky as a bargaining chip for her father. Dumb Blonde: While there's not enough information to justify this, shewasmessing with the amazing Krudsky, and eventually got caught, leading to his rise to power and the near-downfall of the world. Fairy Sexy: She's essentiallyTinkerbellinXenacosplay. Karmic Nod: Willow accepts her father's punishment of being grounded for a whole year without argument seeing as how her sneaking out early was the cause of all the havoc. It probably helps that immediately after setting her punishment, the Goblin King assures her that he is glad to have her back.

characters.name: The Amazing Krudsky
characters.description: A stage magician who is looking for a way to become a real magician. Bald of Evil: He is a bald villain. Big Bad: The true main antagonist of the film, who schemes to obtain real magic. Disproportionate Retribution: Played with. He wants to get back at Scooby and Shaggy because they ruined his performance, but they did it because he wouldn't let Scooby in. Not to mention that he was a real jerk about it. And then obviously trying to take over the world and turning the gang aside from Shaggy and Scooby into monsters put him intoEvil Is Pettyterritory. Fat Bastard: Is a heavyset guy who is theBig Badand becomes MUCH worse when he starts to gain more magical powers, especially when he gets his hands on The Goblin Scepter.

characters.name: Glob & Glum
characters.description: Two of the Goblin King's faithful, yet bumbling shadow goblin minions, featured inScooby-Doo! and the Goblin King. Bumbling Henchmen Duo: They're the Goblin King's two minions who are never seen apart. Card-Carrying Villain: They appear as antagonists, but they're working for the Goblin King, who's not evil. They probably don't know this, though. Expy: OfBogel and WeerdandCrunch and Brunch, two other pairs of bumbling supernatural minions that Scooby and Shaggy dealt with in the past. They're also expies for Jim and Andy, the two characters that were played by Belushi and Campbell onAccording to Jim. Fat and Skinny: Glob and Glum, respectively.

characters.name: Mr. Gibbles
characters.description: The owner of 'Mr. Gibbles' Genuine Magic Shoppe'. Ambiguously Human: He LOOKS human, but he also hasPointy Earsand knows an awful lot about magic. Forced Transformation: He gets turned into a rabbit by Krudsky. He's restored at the end of the movie.

characters.name: Gryphon
characters.description: Big Bad: Serves as this for the film, terrorizing Whirlen Merlin's magic school. "Scooby-Doo" Hoax: Based off a legend surrounding O'Flannery Castle and remotely controlled by Marlon Merlin in order to scare everyone away from the castle, which would force his brother Whirlen (whom he's jealous of due to Whirlen always getting the credit for everything) into selling the place, letting Marlon use the money to start his own magic act.

characters.name: Madelyn Dinkley
characters.description: Velma's younger sister who attends the Whirlen Merlin Magic Academy. Bespectacled Cutie: She, like her sister Velma, wears glasses and is quite the sweetheart. Big Little Sister: Even though she's younger, she's slightly taller than Velma. Break the Cutie: Poor Madelyn falls victim to this trope being trapped in a tower by the Gryphon. The Cameo: She briefly appears in a flashback inFrankencreepy.

characters.name: Whirlen Merlin
characters.description: A magician who founded the Whirlen Merlin Magic Academy. Despair Event Horizon: When the griffin attacking the school drives away his business, he becomes desperate enough to sell the castle to Curdles. Innocently Insensitive: He's a decent guy who does appreciate his brother (even explicitly pointing out Marlon as the brains behind the act), but his constantly showing Marlon up inspires a lot of jealousy and he's blind to this.

characters.name: Marlon Merlin
characters.description: Whirlen Merlin's older brother. Alliterative Name:MarlonMerlin. Dude, Where's My Respect?: He shows some frustration that Merlin gets the applause for their tricks (and the dinner for their guests) despite his substantial contributions. The Eeyore: He can be pretty cynical, and visibly unhappy, and openly talks about the griffin attacks. Gadgeteer Genius: He makes a lot of impressive tricks, not to mention creating the griffin puppet and the blimp that carried it, along with renovating the Griffin's Roost and repairing the old mechanisms inside it.

characters.name: Crystal
characters.description: Death Glare: Gives one toCalvin Curdleswhen she sees him arriving. Friend to All Living Things: Trains the animal assistants, even a lion. Head-Turning Beauty: Fred falls pretty head over heels for her. Implied Love Interest: Her relationship with Whirlin is a bit vague and could just be professional, but she did leave the stage to help him run the school and is sitting next to him protectively at times. Lovely Assistant: Both on the stage and off it.

characters.name: Calvin Curdles
characters.description: An ice cream chain owner trying to buy the castle. Alliterative Name:CalvinCurdles. Grand Romantic Gesture: He wants to buy the castleasone — so he can gift it to Ms. Rumblebuns, the woman he loves. Heel–Face Turn: After Velma exposes his love for Ms. Rumblebuns, he not only confesses it to (and kisses) the latter, but later willingly sponsors the reopening of the Merlin Brothers' Academy of Magic for the magic show in the end. Self-Made Man: Curdles' background. He used to struggle with an ice cream cart and now, thanks to his hard work, owns a big ice cream business.

characters.name: Amos
characters.description: The school's gardener. Doomsayer: He frightens the students with his talk of the Gryphon. The Mole: He's a spy for Calvin. Although he comes across as more of aPunch-Clock Villain, standing to face the Gryphon during the final battle and attending the Merlin brothers magic show at the end.

characters.name: Alma Rumblebuns
characters.description: The caretaker and housekeeper of the castle since before Whirlen bought it. Agent Mulder: She believes the griffin is real and bringing back real magic. Brawn Hilda: A thick-armed woman who stands pretty tall. Crusty Caretaker: A female version. Oblivious to Love: She brushes off Calvin's flirtations as mere flattery despite how long they've known each other and he's shown a clear interest in her. Though, she may have been upset that they haven't seen each other for a long time.

characters.name: Treena and Sherman
characters.description: Birdwatchers who see the griffin return. Even Nerds Have Standards: While she does like birdwatching, Treena would prefer to do something romantic with Sherman. Girly Girl with a Tomboy Streak: While Treena indicates she does like birds and the outdoors, she makes it clear that she sees watching a movie together as a better choice of a date. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: Downplayed, but Treena seems to be about a head taller than Sherman. Intro-Only Point of View: They appear for about two minutes, in the beginning, see the griffin, flee in terror and then disappear from the movie.

characters.name: The Woodsman, the Fishman, and the Specter
characters.description: The three antagonists featured inScooby-Doo: Camp Scare. The Woodsman is anax maniac, the Fishman is a half-fish half-man who lives in the lake, and the Specter of Shadow Canyon is a banshee that haunts Shadow Canyon. Absurdly Sharp Claws: The Specter's claws are sharp enough to graze the side of a metal jeep and reduce a book Scooby uses as a shield to skull-shaped cutouts. Ax-Crazy: A literal example with the Woodsman who swings his axe like he's Santa Claus giving out presents. Chekhov's Skill: Knudsen using the zipline to dress up as the banshee. Family-Unfriendly Death:The Woodsman's backstory at the beginning of the movie is described as gruesomely violent, having suffered a lot of physical trauma after falling down a cliff.The Specter is rumoured to be the wrathful spirit of a hiker who got lost in Shadow Canyon and presumably died from severe starvation/dehydration/heatsroke.

characters.name: Jessica
characters.description: A counselor at Camp Big Moose, seen only inScooby-Doo: Camp Scare. Ambiguously Brown: She has tanned skin. Her voice actress is Asian, so she may be Asian, but she could also be Latina or black. Brainy Brunette: She's dark-haired and a pretty smart girl. Damsel in Distress: The Woodsman has her at his mercy twice in the film, requiring the Gang to help save her. Impossible Hourglass Figure: She is extremely attractive, with an athletic body.

characters.name: Ranger Knudsen
characters.description: A forest ranger seen throughoutScooby-Doo: Camp Scare. Turns out to be the Woodsman, the Fishman, and the Banshee. Abhorrent Admirer: He flirts with Velma. She is revolted by it. Adults Are Useless: Every time the gang tries to report something to him, he doesn't care. Probably because he didn't want them getting suspicious. Affably Evil: Played With. He flirts with Velma, and even tries to clear everybody out of the camp before blowing the dam and flooding the place. On the other hand, he's also responsible for most of the monster encounters, and the things he does would probably qualify as reckless endangerment if not outright attempted murder. Dirty Cop: A forest ranger variant.

characters.name: Luke
characters.description: One of the campers at Camp Little Moose. Abhorrent Admirer: When Trudy claims that Camp Big Moose has the cute boys Camp Little Moose lacks, he pops up beside her as though trying to get her attention and she ignores him. His apparent attraction to her and her lack of reciprocation never come up again, though. The Ace: He easily excels at all the camp's activities, which disappoints Fred because he was hoping to mentor the kid. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: A nice kid with a head full of blonde hair.

characters.name: Trudy
characters.description: One of the campers at Camp Little Moose. Character Development: She becomes less introverted and more open throughout the movie. Chekhov's Skill: She mentions to Velma that her parents sent her to camp because they think she spends too much time on the computer at home. Her computer skills come in handy later when she's able to hack some stolen sonar equipment to reveal that the villains were searching for something at the bottom of Camp Big Moose's lake. Commonality Connection: She and Velma hit it off well given that they're both somewhat unwilling to be roughing it. Velma's counseling helps Trudy to begin enjoying herself. Deadpan Snarker: Probably the snarkiest character in the movie.

characters.name: Deacon/Babyface Boretti
characters.description: A kid who comes to Camp Little Moose over the summer inScooby-Doo: Camp Scare. Turns out to be a criminal trying to get them to leave the campsite so that they won't die when he and Knudsen blow the dam and flood the place. Bald of Evil: He's secretly a criminal and he turns out to be bald. Big Bad: Think about it. Between him and Knudsen, whose idea was it to evacuate the camp before flooding it? Even Evil Has Standards: Still tried evacuating the camp before flooding it. Karmic Butt-Monkey: He takes the most comical battering during the film, even topping Shaggy and Scooby. It becomes karmic in retrospect once he reveals himself as the mastermind.

characters.name: Burt
characters.description: The owner of Camp Little Moose. Big Damn Heroes: Burt and Daphne swoop down on zip lines to yank Fred and Velma away from the ax-wielding Woodsman. Big Fun: Burt has a noticeable gut and is a warm-hearted man who cares about giving his campers a fun experience and keeping them safe. Sixth Ranger: Burt accompanies the gang for most of the investigation.

characters.name: Darryl
characters.description: Burt's assistant,at least until the monsters show up. Expy: Of Crazy Ralph fromFriday the 13th (1980), as both of them act as a doomsayer who spreads warnings about anAx-Crazyvillain. The Prankster: He dresses up as campfire story villain The Woodsman to scare some campers. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: He runs away in terror when he sees The Woodsman and packs up his bags and heads off to Camp Big Moose the next morning. Took a Level in Jerkass: He's a good-natured counselor in his first scene and later warns the gang about the danger before fleeing Camp Little Moose. However, upon getting a job at Camp Big Moose, he angrily confronts Shaggy and Scooby for not being from Camp Big Moose (even though they're invited guests) and doesn't intervene when his campers pelt them with food.

characters.name: The Phantosaur
characters.description: The main antagonist ofScooby-Doo! Legend of the Phantosaur. Has two forms; the original form is a large, glowing, tangible dinosaur, and the second form is made completely of fire, also with the ability to breathe fire. Big Bad: The Phantosaur is this for the film as it is the main monster that Mystery Inc is trying to solve regarding its mysterious presence. Dinosaurs Are Dragons: The Fiery Phantosaur can breathe fire, in addition to being made of it. Hologram: The Fiery Phantosaur is only a projection created with 3D computer graphics. Man in the Machine: The original Phantosaur was being robotically controlled.

characters.name: Professor Svankmajer
characters.description: A paleontologist featured inScooby-Doo! Legend of the Phantosaur. Affably Evil: She confesses to the game pretty calmly and politely when she's caught, and immediately helps everyone escape when the tunnels start collapsing by telling everyone about the riskier second exit after the safe one collapses. Bad Liar: To the point where it's lampshaded by the gang. Her acting and delivery are perfectly believable but she loses points for talking about how Winsor had already left the dig when his car is still there, and in plain sight. Big Bad: She is this for the second half. As she is using the fiery Phantosaur as part of her scheme to bring the crystal of the allosaurus out in the night with the town empty. Casual Danger Dialogue: During the attack of the original Phantosaur (the one she wasn't behind) she just stands around thoughtfully musing about several of its physical traits in comparison to what she'd expected to form a dinosaur.of course, she later claims that she had realized that the original phantosaur was a fake from the beginning.

characters.name: Winsor
characters.description: A teenager who assists Professor Svankmajer with her paleontological dig. He also assists her in the creation of the Fiery Phantosaur. Seen inScooby-Doo! Legend of the Phantosaur. Chekhov's Skill: His first scene mentions that he took computer animation classes, which he uses on the dinosaur. Does Not Like Spam: He doesn't like salmon eggs, which is one thing he turns out to have in common with Velma. Geeky Turn-On: He and Velma were instantly attracted when they met at the dig. They discussed dinosaur fossils and discovered they had a lot in common. Romantic False Lead: To Velma, though Velma was still attracted to him in the end, and said she would date him again after he got out of jail.

characters.name: Mr. Hubley
characters.description: The man who owns the spa that the gang comes to visit inScooby-Doo! Legend of the Phantosaur. Accidental Misnaming: He doesn't get any of the gang's names right. Cloudcuckoolander: He seems distracted; he can't get Shaggy's nickname right, for example. Cool Old Guy: He's an old man who owns a spa and is a master of hypnotism. Honest Corporate Executive: He mentions that he would have liked it if the locals had sold him more land to expand his spa, but finds the idea of dressing up like a ghost to scare them off laughable.

characters.name: Shakey Joe
characters.description: A man who runs a coffee business, seen inScooby-Doo! Legend of the Phantosaur. Klatchian Coffee: His business is sellingverystrong coffees, as seen when Scooby drinks some and becomes hyperactive. He evidently drinks a lot of it too, given how shaky and jittery he is most of the time. Meaningful Name: The "shakey" bit of his name refers to the fact he always shakes and jitters. Wide Eyes and Shrunken Irises: Due to being constantly buzzed on his own very strong coffee, his eyes are always wide with no apparent irises.

characters.name: Tex
characters.description: Tex is the leader of the motorcycle gang Shaggy beat up at "Faith's All You Can Eat" in La Serena. Badass Biker: He's a cool biker. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He's very intimidating at first, but helps Shaggy save his friends in the end. Worthy Opponent: He respects Shaggy after the latter bests him in the race.

characters.name: Ms. Deitch and Mr. Babbit
characters.description: Mining company executives who want the paleontologists gone to dig up a new silver vein. Affably Evil: They never end up hurting anyone and take being exposed fairly well. Bantering Baddie Buddies: They always appear together and have some sinister banter. Big Bad Duumvirate: They serve as this for the first half of the film. They were using a green Phantosaur for their scheme in order to dig in the mine by using it to shut down their dig. Corrupt Corporate Executive: They try to shut down the dig to further their mine.

characters.name: Marius Brancusi
characters.description: The owner of the Brancusi Circus. Seen inBig Top Scooby-Doo!. Bound and Gagged: He gets tied up and gagged twice in the movie. Failed a Spot Check: Somehow he thinks that garlic works against werewolves, not vampires. Nice Guy: Likes entertaining people with his circus. Red Herring: He's one of the suspects, and his behavior is a little suspicious, but Archambault was just trying to frame him.

characters.name: Archambault
characters.description: A French-Canadian strongman that travels with the Brancusi Circus inBig Top Scooby-Doo!. Bad People Abuse Animals: He's shown to not mind cruelty toward animals. "Archambault never punch a horse before.Could be fun!" Big Bad: He is the arch-villain of the movie. Dumb Muscle: Averted. Despite how he speaks, he's as cunning as he is strong. Muscles Are Meaningful: He has big muscles to show he is strong.

characters.name: Oliverio & Lena
characters.description: Two German trapeze artists seen throughoutBig Top Scooby-Doo!. Crazy Jealous Guy: Oliverio becomes jealous of Fred when Lena flirts with him. Everyone Has Standards: Oliverio states he won't actually, intentionally drop Fred during their act, as doing so would hurt his reputation. Impossible Hourglass Figure: Lena has an athletic build. Mother Russia Makes You Strong: Though, they're supposed to be German.

characters.name: Whitney Doubleday
characters.description: The animal trainer who travels with the Brancusi Circus. Even Evil Has Standards: While he was willing to work with Archambault, he tells Shaggy and Scooby (after first meeting them) that he'd never do anything to hurt any of the animals within the Brancusi Circus. Flat Character: There's nothing much to this guy other than him appearing in one scene at the beginning before going missing and helping Archambault with his plan. Gender-Blender Name: While "Whitney" can be used as a man's name, it's considerably more common as a woman's name. Gracefully Demoted: He tells the gang that he doesn't mind being forced into retirement due to how he's getting old for the job anyway and understands the backlash against animal acts due to how many animal acts are abusive and exploitative.it turns out he's lying though.

characters.name: Wulfric von Rydingsvard
characters.description: A heavy metal rock singer seen inBig Top Scooby-Doo!. Cloudcuckoolander: He claims to be a werewolf and even some of his employees admit he has a tenuous grasp on reality. How They Treat the Help: He thanks his assistant Phil for saving his life. Informed Ability: He is a famous rock star, but when the audience finally hears his music, it doesn't quite sound like it's worth the hype. Red Herring: Everywhere his band traveled there have been werewolf attacks. That's because they wanted the black diamond he wears.

characters.name: Schmatko
characters.description: But Now I Must Go: Leaves the circus to follow his real dreams at the end. Classically Trained Extra: He's an actor who finds clowning beneath him. Fat and Skinny: The fat to Sisko's skinny. Gleeful and Grumpy Pairing: The Grumpy to Sisko's Gleeful. We Hardly Knew Ye: Disappears, presumably turned into a werewolf, after just one scene.

characters.name: Sisko
characters.description: Ambiguous Syntax: Once Schmatko leaves the circus, Sisko comments he thought he'd never leave, but whether or not this is meant as aHidden Disdain Revealor simply surprise that his colleague finally did leave to follow his dreams is unclear. Fat and Skinny: He's the skinny to Schmatko's fat. Gleeful and Grumpy Pairing: The Gleeful to Schmatko's Grumpy. Suddenly Voiced: He mostly communicates by blowing an air horn but does comment on Schmatko leaving.

characters.name: Phil Flaxman
characters.description: One of Wulfric's employees. Badass Bystander: The only one of Wulfric's posse to try and help him when the werewolf is stealing his necklace. First-Name Basis: He claims that even his kids call him Phil.

characters.name: Austin
characters.description: A kid who hangs around the convention and is friendly to the Scooby gang. Distressed Dude: At one point near the end, he's attacked by the villains, forcing Scooby-Doo to go intoHeroic Dogmode to rescue him. Tagalong Kid: He's mainly just a youngster who hangs around with Shaggy and Scooby.

characters.name: Jennifer Severin
characters.description: The producer of the newDarker and EdgierBlue Falcon movie. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Jennifer's love for putting "revenge" in the titles of her movies and her glee at blowing things up instead of having a real story makes her a very unflattering reference to Michael Bay. Pet the Dog: She does eventually give Owen a cameo appearance in her new movie. Red Herring: Shaggy points out that she's happy about all the publicity the Hyde attacks are creating for the new movie, but she's not behind them.

characters.name: Owen Garrison
characters.description: The original Blue Falcon, who is not happy about the reboot. Advertised Extra: Despite Blue Falcon being seen on the film cover, being on equal footing with the rest of the cast (or Shaggy and Scooby at least), the man who played Blue Falcon is only in a small handful of scenes. Justified in that he's mostly there trying to prove his worth of being the original Blue Falcon and is a fall guy for the real culprit. Dude, Where's My Respect?: Shaggy and Scooby-Doo are the only ones to have nothing but respect and admiration for him. Hero with Bad Publicity: Sadly, Mr. Garrison was swindled out of the rights to the Blue Falcon and was not even allowed to wear the character's costume for years. It gets even worse after he becomes a prime suspect in the Hyde attacks, thanks to his public disdain about the new movie. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Mr. Garrison may be grouchy, but he's no more a villain than the guy he played. He was not behind the attacks, despite his dislike of the reboot, and he even pulls a last-minute save when Scooby is attacked by the Hyde Hound.

characters.name: Cuthbert Crawley
characters.description: The family lawyer of the Dinkley family, who is actually the gang's old enemy Cuthbert Crawls, one of the two people who masqueraded as the Phantom Shadows from theoriginal seriesepisode "A Night of Fright is No Delight". Clark Kenting: He's Cuthbert Crawls and all he did to disguise himself as the Dinkleys' family lawyer was simply wear glasses and slightly change his surname. The gang didn't figure out the connection until the last act of the film. Significant Double Casting: Inspector Krunch is him in disguise. Suddenly Speaking: Cuthbert Crawls never said a word in his original appearance.

characters.name: Mrs. Vanders
characters.description: The caretaker and housekeeper of Castle Von Dinkenstein, who is actually the gang's old enemy Mama Mione, the culprit from theScooby-Doo Showepisode "The Creepy Case of Old Iron Face" in disguise. Cast as a Mask: Not only is she voiced by a different person than the woman underneath the mask, she's voiced by a man! Kinda surprised it wasn't a guy underneath the disguise, too. Mama Mione herself is voiced by Grey Griffin. Creepy Housekeeper: Fits the bill to a tee. Not surprising as her character is an amalgam of famous versions of this trope. Gass Hole: She passes gas a large number of times throughout the movie. Mama Mione apparently didn't fake this, as she even drops onewhile being taken awayduring the credits, with an officer reacting like he just witnessed a murder. Germanic Depressives: She's incredibly melancholic, snarky and apathetic while around the gang. It's only when she's out of view she shows any emotion. Also, did I forget to mention the incredibly thick German accent Mama Mione uses while disguised?

characters.name: Baron Basil von Dinkenstein
characters.description: Velma Dinkley's notorious great-great-uncle, who allegedly created a hideousFrankenstein's Monsterknown as Frankencreep and is established as the inspiration for Mary Shelley writing her famous novelFrankenstein. Dr. Fakenstein: Being a Victor Frankenstein pastiche is justified, considering that it's established that his alleged experiments inspired Mary Shelley to write the original book. Mad Scientist: The legend states that he was an insane scientist who tried to create his ownFrankenstein's Monster. Posthumous Character: Being an ancestor of Velma Dinkley, it's a given that he's long dead by the events of the film. The Von Trope Family: His surname has "von" in front of it.

characters.name: AlexSuperFan2112
characters.description: A fan (if a bit critical one) of the gang's exploits. Butt-Monkey: Particularly when the end credits show him getting arrested for pointing out the movie's continuity errors. Nerd Glasses: He's bespectacled and a bit of a geek.

characters.name: Delilah Domino
characters.description: The head of security at KISS World. Alliterative Name:DelilahDomino. Big Bad: Arguably, as technically the Destroyer was the main threat. But that is an entire worm-hole on it's own that the film itself doesn't explain. Caught by Arrogance: Stupidly bragged about her power as head of security, as well as hiding her stolen loot in her UNLOCKED locker. Fanservice Costumes: While her regular uniform doesn't fit the bill (unless your fetish is fully clad police women), her disguise as the Crimson Witch certainly does.

characters.name: Shandi Strutter
characters.description: The effects designer for KISS. Alliterative Name:ShandiStrutter. Nice Girl: She's generally patient and encouraging The Reliable One: She's very reliable and helpful to both the band and the gang throughout the investigation. Shout-Out: Her names come from two of the band's songs.

characters.name: ChipMcGhoo
characters.description: Ink-Suit Actor: Is a slightly renamed and largely similar-looking guy to KISS's real manager, who provides his voice.

characters.name: Scarecrow/Jonathan Crane
characters.description: An enemy of Batman who is an intelligent scientist. Ambiguous Situation: Because Scooby-Doo crossed over with Batman in the past and because of how Scooby-Doo is loose with its canon, it's never stated if he's fromBrave and the Boldor another take of the character. Composite Character: He takes elements from the various incarnations of Scarecrow, such as the '90s animated. But also elements from Jack fromThe Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandyas Maxell Atoms wrote the special. Mainly how he uses a scythe and has a parade of mutated pumpkins attacking the city (though they are revealed to be drones). Multilayer Façade: Crane wears a jack o' lantern over his Scarecrow mask. Rogues' Gallery Transplant: He's traditionally an antagonist to the superheroBatman. Here, he crosses blades with Mystery Inc.

characters.name: Coco Diablo
characters.description: The costume designer who created all the monster costumes that Mystery Inc. faced in their entire careers. Balance Between Good and Evil: Seems to believe in this, as she suggests that the "phantoms" the gang are dealing with are a result of their meddling upsetting that balance. Card-Carrying Villain: While giving a customer a tour of her business at the start of the episode, she brings out a costume based on herself and describes the look as "Treacherous Maven", then calls down "her office" that's set up inside a fake devil's head. Heel–Face Turn: She goes from evil fashion designer to friend for the Mystery Inc. gang. She gives them costumes to wear while rounding up the escaped convicts and she forces the criminals to hand over the candy they stole. She also seems to reciprocate Velma's affections before she goes back to prison. The Man Behind the Man: She was the one who made all of the costumes used by the many criminals Mystery Inc. unmasked and put away over the years.

characters.name: Krypto the Superdog
characters.description: Animal Superhero: He's a dog but has Superman's powers and the intelligence to use them to fight evil. Deuteragonist: Outside of the gang, he's the character who gets the most focus. Kryptonite Factor: Being Kryptonian, he's vulnerable to the stuff just like Superman. Luthor takes advantage of this by building a canine version of Metallo, Rex Ruthor, to blast Krypto with the poisonous radiation. Super-Speed: At one point, he eats some of Shaggy and Scooby's snacks in seconds with a couple of speedy-to-the-point-of-invisible passes. Super-Strength: He's powerful enough to knock over Solomon Grundy with no problem.

characters.name: TheDaily Planet
characters.description: Camera Fiend: When Lois asks Jimmy if he brought his camera, he thinks it's as obvious as if she'd asked whether he brought his eyes. Crossover Ship:In-Universe; Jimmy has a crush on Daphne and the two were labeled "Best Redheaded Couple" at a camp they attended as kids. Daphne is more exasperated that neither he nor Fred will let it go. Decoy Protagonist: DecoyDeuteragonist, to be exact. Lois Lane and Jimmy Olsen are prominently featured inThe Teaserand are seemingly set up to help Mystery Inc. with the investigation, but they end up staying out of it and are never seen again until the mystery is over, leaving Krypto as the true deuteragonist of the movie. Intrepid Reporter: They go investigating in the Hall of Justice after the League disappears, hoping to find some clue about what happened. Jimmy actually pauses before fleeing from one of the phantoms to snap a few pictures for confirmation. Self-Proclaimed Love Interest: Jimmy apparently lied to Lois that he and Daphne were dating, despite the latter's protests. He eventually calls it off at the end of the movie.

characters.name: Lex Luthor
characters.description: Bald of Evil: As usual, he's hairless and a major pain to the heroes. Big Bad: Although his henchwoman Mercy Graves drives most of the plot, he takes over the position of main villain from her during the climax. However, given that she took on the lead mantle due to thinking Lex had become "soft", she's not very unhappy. Evil Overlord: His plan involves using an army of robots to take over Metropolis. Hijacked by Ganon: Heisthe Ganon. After Lex Luthor's assistant Mercy Graves is revealed to be the culprit behind the mystery, Luthor takes over her scheme as theFinal Boss, having known about it all along.

characters.name: Mercy Graves
characters.description: Big Bad:She is the Big Bad for most of the film since she is the own behind everything in the film such as the disappearance of the Justice League, the scaring on Metropolis' citizens, and the villains rampaging. Demoted to Dragon:She was theBig Badfor most of the film but once Lex reveals his true colors to Mystery Inc and Krypto, she helps him with his plans. Disc-One Final Boss:She ends up being this to Luthor. As she was revealed to be responsible for most of the plot in the film, Lex ends up using her plans for his own ends and therefore becomes theFinal Bossof the film. The Dragon: She is this to Lex in the film. The Heavy:She is the one drives most of the plot as she is the one responsible for the members of the Justice League’s disappearance in the first place. She believed Lex has become too "soft" for his own good.

characters.name: Old Man Smithers / The Luna Ghost
characters.description: The janitor of the Wow-O Toy Factory. Adaptational Nice Guy: In the video game, Old Man Smithers helps Mystery Inc. and didn't threaten them. Advertised Extra: He is shown in promotional material including the film's poster in spite of being quickly defeated and carried away by the authorities in the beginning of the film. Canon Immigrant: The Luna Ghost's costume can be seen in the first episode ofScooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated. Celeb Crush: WithPamela Anderson. He apparently committed his crime over her turning him down for a date.

characters.name: Mary Jane
characters.description: A college student who falls in love with Shaggy. Beauty Equals Goodness: She is both beautiful and polite to her friends. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Unlike the other characters that originated in the first film, she is the only one not mentioned in the sequel. Getting Crap Past the Radar: Her name is a normal (albeit somewhat old-fashioned) name, but it's also one of themanynames of marijuana. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Mary Jane is kind and sweet to everyone, as well as sharing Shaggy's love of food.

characters.name: Emile Mondavarious
characters.description: The founder of the Spooky Island theme park that was imprisoned by Scrappy-Doo. Impersonation-Exclusive Character: He actually only appeared at the very end of the film. The Mondavarious we saw before that was actually Scrappy in a robotic suit. Sir Not-Appearing-in-This-Trailer: Both he and the robot double of him Scrappy-Doo used as a disguise were kept hidden by the marketing.

characters.name: N'Goo Tuana
characters.description: The leader of Scrappy-Doo's forces in Spooky Island. Bald of Evil: He is bald and is working with Scrappy to carry out his evil plans. The Dragon: Second-in-command to Scrappy-Doo. Mr. Exposition: N'Goo explained the origins of Spooky Island to the visitors. Sir Not-Appearing-in-This-Trailer: He never appears in the trailers.

characters.name: Voodoo Maestro
characters.description: A voodoo practitioner at Spooky Island. Cuckoosnarker: He's as snarky as he is strange, which is saying a lot from a guy who tried to sacrifice a dead chicken."Purple is a fall color, it's the middle of May!" Hollywood Voodoo: His voodoo practicing is rather inaccurate.It does serve to make him look even stranger. No Name Given: Mystery Inc. didn't get a chance to learn his name. Reverse Psychology: Averted. Daphnethinkshe's trying to use this to get her to go to the Spooky Island castle, even though he is indeed telling the truth.

characters.name: Zarkos
characters.description: A Mexican wrestler employed by Scrappy-Doo and N'Goo Tuana. Gratuitous Spanish: He referred to Daphne as "Senorita". Hidden Depths: Zarkos is a Telemundo celebrity before he joined Scrappy and N'Goo Tuana. Masked Luchador: One who used to appear in Mexican soaps. Oh, Crap!: He received this moment as he was cornered and defeated by Daphne, making him the damsel in distress.

characters.name: Melvin Doo
characters.description: A college student who visited Spooky Island. Brick Joke: He first thought that he received a phone call when it turns out Scooby has to answer it. When Scrappy revealed his intentions to absorb Scooby's soul, Scooby tried to ask if he meant Melvin. Chekhov's Gag: He's introduced in a brief gag as a human who inexplicably shares his surname with Scooby, then is randomly brought up again by Scooby when Scrappy reveals that he plans to absorb Scooby's soul. The Generic Guy: The only thing special about him is the fact that he shares his last name with Scooby.

characters.name: Demons
characters.description: The inhabitants of Spooky Island. Actor Allusion:Frank Welkervoices agroup of creaturesthat get killed by sunlight. Demonic Possession: They extract a person's soul and then step into the body to possess them. Expy: The Demons are based onthe Gremlins; Due to having similar reptilian designs, and the same weakness to sunlight. Even helps thatFrank Welkervoiced both the Demons and Gremlins. Laughably Evil: They're pretty terrifying, but between their incompetent bumbling, slapstick abuse, andpoor attempts at acting like college students, they're also funny to watch.

characters.name: Dr. Jonathan Jacobo / Evil Masked Figure / Heather Jasper Howe
characters.description: AMad Scientistwho wanted to created monsters. Adaptational Goal Change: InThe Scooby-Doo Show, Johnny was donning the Pterodactyl Ghost disguise to cover up a music-pirating operation in remote canyons. In the movie's backstory, Dr. Jonathan Jacobo was using the disguise in the city to commit bank robberies so he could fund his early experiments to createrealmonsters. Adaptational Intelligence: He started out as the Pterodactyl Ghost, one of the monsters Mystery, Inc. faced inThe Scooby-Doo Show. The incarnation in the original cartoon was not a scientist. Adapted Out: In the PC video game, Dr. Jacobo is never seen andboth Heather Jasper Howe and the Evil Masked Figure are two different characters. Ambiguous Gender Identity: Jacobo spends the majority ofMonsters Unleasheddisguised as (and, if the serum Shaggy drinks by accident is anything to go by,physically transformed into) a woman, when a male disguise probably would have served him just as well. He commits to the role of Heather Jasper Howe hard enough to have entered into an implicit relationship with (the presumably straight) Ned. Jacobo also boasts about having been an "excellent"Elizain a performance ofMy Fair Lady.

characters.name: Patrick Wisely
characters.description: The curator of the Coolsonian Criminology Museum. Beware the Nice Ones: He's a genuinely nice, if somewhat awkward guy, but when his museum is being put at stake he can actually be quite threatening. Large Ham: While he interrogated a man about the second museum robbery. Nerd Glasses: He wears glasses and is geeky. Red Herring: There are a couple of scenes that are set up to make him look like the culprit. He gets into a fight with someone outside the Faux Ghost and Velma catches him in a secret room with a lot of artifacts on Johnathan Jacobo.

characters.name: Jeremiah Wickles
characters.description: The former identity of the Black Knight Ghost. Affably Evil: Unlike Dr. Jacobo, he is aware that there is still good inside him. Evil Old Folks: He's an elderly man who Mystery Inc. unmasked in the past. Because of his arrest, he has a reason to seek out revenge towards the Mystery Inc. Eye Scream: He threatened to tear Mystery Inc.'s eyes out of their skulls and make them eat the eyes. Heel–Face Turn: Is seen partying with the cast at the end, so he probably let bygones be bygones after the gang cleared his name.

characters.name: The Black Knight Ghost
characters.description: AnAnimated Armorand the second monster brought to life that the gang faces. Adaptational Dye-Job: The plume on his helmet is red in the original cartoon. Here, it's black. Adaptational Name Change: A minor case. In the original cartoon, he was simply called the Black Knight. This version is called the Black Knight Ghost. Animated Armor: He is basically an armor brought to life by the Evil Masked Figure. Attack Its Weak Point:Parodied. As Daphne is frantically fighting the Black Knight, Velma is trying to decipher his weakness by reading an overly complicated paragraph in an ancient book and when she finally figures it out, she goes ahead annnnd...she kicks him in the groin, which manages to incapacitate him.

characters.name: Pterodactyl Ghost
characters.description: The first monster brought to life by the Evil Masked Figure. Co-Dragons: It and the Black Knight Ghost serve as the main enforcers of the Evil Masked Figure, doing most of the dirty work for him such as stealing the suits necessary for making more monsters. The Dreaded: The Pterodactyl Ghost is easily the most threatening villain in the movie besides theBig Bad. While it may not have a dangerous weapon like the Black Knight or unlimited destructive power like the 10,000 Volt Ghost and the Tar Monster, it makes up for it by being aLightning BruiserSuper-Persistent Predatorwhich comesveryclose to killing at least one member of Mystery Inc. every time they have to deal with it.Daphne even calls it "the dreaded Pterodactyl Ghost" in the opening scene. Early-Bird Cameo: The Pterodactyl Ghost can be seen flying through Coolsville in the opening of the movie and disappearing into the sewers before being properly introduced attacking the museum. Help, I'm Stuck!: Ends up trapped inside the Tar Monster when it accidentally charges into him during the final battle.

characters.name: Tar Monster
characters.description: A monster literally made out of tar, he is one of the four that Scooby and Shaggy accidentally release. Adaptational Badass: The original Tar Monster left tar tracks everywhere, but he couldn't control the tar or his shape and size. Here, the Tar Monster is aOne-Man Armywho can not only do those things, but is arguablyone of the most dangerous and threatening monsters on the team. Adaptation Dye-Job: The original Tar Monster's eye was pure green, here he has a white cornea and a blue iris. Blob Monster: He's just a very big blob of tar. Curb-Stomp Battle: Believe it or not, on the RECEIVING end of one curtesy of Scooby-Doo. While he was by far the most powerful of the remaining monsters by the final battle, even coming close to being the monster to actually kill the gang, once Scooby finds a fire extinguisher, Scooby effortlessly beats back Tar Monster by freezing his tar. It's so easy for Scooby that he doesn't even bother trying to avoid the Tar Monster's attack as he literally stops them in place the moment Tar Monster tries, even grinding on the frozen tar for fun as if he was skateboarding. Even when Tar Monster attacks face to face, he isn't fast enough for Scooby and Scooby freezes his whole body breaks him apart.

characters.name: Skeleton Men
characters.description: A pair of skeleton henchmen that are always seen together, they are the fourth and fifth monsters to be brought to life. Adaptational Comic Relief: The Skeleton Men were originally ominously eerie villains in the cartoon, but here they're aStupid Evilduo who always fail at their objectives. Adaptational Species Change: The original Skeleton Men were obviously humans wearing jumpsuits with a skeleton design on them. Here, they areliteralwalking skeletons. Ballistic Bone: As they are chasing Velma during the climax of the film, the red-eyed skeleton detaches the head of the green one and launches it at her.It fails, leaving the head of his friend stuck in a wall. Boke and Tsukkomi Routine: The red-eyed Skeleton Man is the tsukkomi to the green-eyed Skeleton Man's boke.

characters.name: 10, 000 Volt Ghost
characters.description: A giant monster made out of electricity, presumably the third monster to be brought to life. Adaptational Badass: In the original cartoon, the most it was shown to do was melt a lock with a single touch. Here, it's a full-fledged electrical monster which is shown to be one of the most dangerous and can jump between electrical appliances. Bring It: Invokes this when he strikes the typical pose when confronted by Daphne near the end of the film. Defeat Equals Explosion: He explodes after being sucked into the Black Knight Ghost's body by a pair of jumper cables. Diabolus ex Nihilo: His first scene involves him appearing out of nowhere while the gang is being chased by the monstersShaggy and Scooby just created. A deleted scene had a much more proper introduction made for him, which can be found online.

characters.name: Miner 49er
characters.description: One of the monsters accidentally released by Scooby and Shaggy. Adaptational Badass: He wields a pickaxe and can breathe fire from his mouth, two things he never had and couldn't do in the original cartoon.In addition, the original Miner, despite his imposing appearance, wasn't all that dangerous and just simply scared people away. But this Miner is a truly dangerous and battle-ready behemoth. In addition, the original Miner, despite his imposing appearance, wasn't all that dangerous and just simply scared people away. But this Miner is a truly dangerous and battle-ready behemoth. Adaptational Ugliness: The original Miner 49er looked somewhat clean and put together as well as fit and imposing. In the film, the Miner looks less hygienic with bad teeth, a craggier face, anda massive and hairy gut hanging out from his shirt. Ash Face: He gets a burnt up face after Scooby uses his fart to blow his own flames back at him.

characters.name: Captain Cutler's Ghost
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: The original Cutler was aHarmless Villainwho faked his own death and merely scared people away. This Cutler is armed with a speargun and actively tries to kill the gang with it. Advertised Extra: Was on most to all of the promotional material and yet only gets one minute total of screen time. Creepy Old-Fashioned Diving Suit: Keeping his look from his other appearances, he has the display of an ominous diving suit covered by seaweed with a green glow that obscures what is inside of it. Logical Weakness: His gun only holds two spears, so he is unable to defend himself or act much further after firing both of them. Oh, Crap!: His reaction when Fred backs the Mystery Machine into him, knocking him back into the lake.

characters.name: Zombie
characters.description: Adaptational Comic Relief: The original Zombie was a menacing and ominousVoodoo Zombiedoing the bidding of aWicked Witchbefore he was unmasked. The Zombie here is much more comedic with gags of him throwing up on a reporter and getting pantsed by Scooby Doo. Adaptational Ugliness: Downplayed. The original Zombie already looked monsterous, but he was arguably easier on the eyes, wore neater clothing, and stood taller with only a slight hunch in his back. The Zombie here looks much more goblin-like, wears more ragged clothing, and his hunchback ismuchmore prominent. Bald of Evil: He, as one of the monster cronies created from a costume, remains not only bald like his original incarnation, he is also uglier and vomited on a reporter. Flat Character: Is the only one of the monsters that doesn't really do much in the movie except provide some comedic relief. Gonk: Out of all the monsters, he's the one with the goofiest-looking appearance.

characters.name: The Cotton Candy Glob
